item.title: Re: Formatting help
item.content:encoded:
I'd also like to point out that you have one too many open brackets at the beginning of the component code. The whole tool won't work unless the excess bracket is excised. Example:

Original:

 [[[include :smlt:component:aers:classification-stuff |item=6000 |lvl=4 |class=Safe |threat=Yellow |threat-colour=#j01 ]]

Updated:

 [[include :smlt:component:aers:classification-stuff |item= $item |lvl= $lvl |class= $class |threat= $threat |threat-colour= $colour ]]

And, yeah, going off of what Croq said, the color hex to turn the dot yellow would be #ffff00.

item.title: The Evolves (Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Page Layout: Description and containment procedures of the entity | Conversations with the entity | Description and containment procedures of a deadly virus created by the entity.

Elevator Pitch: A new generation of humanity is on the horizon with the ability to connect to any piece of computerized machinery and manipulate its code to their will through their mind and the foundation has found and contained The First.

The First: Has normal teenager appearances. He is the first person to have been spotted with such abilities. Hacks into the foundation database almost everyday in hope to find someone like him (the foundation is close to developing a software to protect their database). Isn't really cooperative due to being separated from his parents and knows that he will never be able to see them. Hobbies include singing, reading fictional books.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Besides the common ability mentioned above. These "Evolves" have a unique ability. "The First" I want this article on has the unique ability to engineer a virus which attacks on the human brain and shuts it down in 2-3 days. When an infected is in contact with any computer, the virus will inject some of its code which will act as a computer virus capable of taking down the entire NASA Database in a single day.

Additional Notes: I have not started a draft on this yet but will do it as soon as/if I get the greenlights required. Would love as many suggestions, critiques on this as I can get.

item.title: Te Horoi Pai
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Mystery

+ show block
– hide block

Elevator Pitch: A tube of Petroleum jelly. When ointment is applied to a human, a person's hygiene is enhanced. Prominent symptom manifest in the form of pheromone secretion and irrational compulsion to spread the ointment. Hours after patient zero is infected, the infected encounter amorphous entities. Appearing entities embody subconscious fetishes or extremest fears. They ignore beings lacking pheromone and are hostile to those marked with pheromone.

Central Narrative: On the 9th December, the mysterious disappearance of 25 guests and staff at the Westhaven Luxury Lodge made national headlines. A team of four Field Agents stationed at Nelson, New Zealand take over the investigation and create a cover story.

Field Agents are briefed about the crime scene by the police. Exploring the lodge they find five rooms in the hallway cordoned off by police tape. Foundation agents are alarmed by the crude messages scratched into the Manuka wood and signs glued onto the walls left behind by the lodging's former occupants. Text advertise and revere "a conditioner sent by the gods". Most jarringly, the other remainder of the text read "The knavish resistance were enlightened, now they too relish the heaven-sent scent". Conditioner called "Te Horoi Pai" , translated to Xtreme Conditioner is discovered and placed in containment. All other copies found in the Lodging or within Police custody are confiscated and destroyed.

Testing is conducted, discovering the anomaly's psycho-contagious nature. It's speculated an unknown G.O.I is at hand. A nationwide sweep, extensively covering every hotel, motel and supermarket in New Zealand, yields negative results. A Mobile Taskforce (Called Bad Hair Day) is conceived to monitor the domestic supply chain for wild instances.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Mass disappearance is unheard-of in the 21st century, creating mystery. The anomaly takes place in New Zealand. Testing reveals the ultimate fate of the Lodging's residents. Furthermore, the G.O.I theory is a hypothesis, since Te Horoi Pai is the product name but there is no brand associated nor a manufacturer stated on the bottle. Therefore, the Foundation attempts to contain a contagious SCP with no identified point of origin; an analogy for viral outbreak clusters with no immediate causes.

Additional Notes: This is a submission for my first "canon" SCP, so any form of criticism is appreciated (Bluntness is 100% tolerated but please be constructive).

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello JackrawTheWriter! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

It's awesome you finally decided to make an account - after all, only by voting, which only people with one can, can you actively affect the quality of works posted onsite. I'm also happy to see you quite want to contribute, too - I can't wait to see what you come up with, I'm sure it will be awesome!

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: Re: Book of the undead
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello! Not an official critter here, but I can still read and give opinions.
And in my opinion this is kinda… nothing? It feels very much like a Series I article and even then a kind of very basic one.
It feels like an "object that does a thing", in this case a 'book that does a revive'.
Nowadays, skips need a bit more than just that to work, I'm afraid.

Specifically, you need a story! Something to make a reader go 'wow, this SCP has something to say for itself! It exists in a world and has a purpose and the conflicts/events it causes do have an effect!".
Or something like that.
What I'm trying to say is- ok, this book revives people. Is it a relic of an ancient civilization? Is it something a guy who could do some supernatural stuff cooked up to resurrect his dead cat? What is that creature, anyway? What's its correlation to the SCP?
Not every SCP Object's gotta kill you dead, after all. I'd argue a few of my favorite skips, in fact, do not do so at all.

These are just a few points you could try answering, and I'm sure as you do more will pop up in your head! Remember, there are no ideas not worth exploring. Even if you don't pursue that thread in the end, it's more worldbuilding- it helps paint a clearer picture of your story in your head!

item.title: Re: Greenlight Concept - Article - Horror / History -Related to Sarkicism & CotBG
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Hmm. I'm not sure how I feel about this as a SCP article: it feels like this really needs a like, historical observer who can tell this story from the outside as the various events happen; I could see perhaps it being a tale from the perspective of the SCP, or perhaps something like a Serpents Hand format?

Really my issue with this as a SCP is that 'the Foundation discovers the anomaly' feels too much like the end of the story than the start, and I'm kinda feeling like the history of the anomaly is the most interesting part? On the flip side, a deep, historical look at this could be very interesting if like, all the investigation is laid out; with the foundation assuming she's a new anomaly and then gradually piecing stuff together to the final ending where they discover who she was originally, y'know?

This ties into my concerns with:

followed by a retrieval log and accompanied by a brief test log with two or three addenda related to the nature of the SCP.

I'm not really sure what your addenda show, but I'm not convinced a test log would be that interesting here at all. I guess really what I want to know is how the narrative and the page layout tie together?

item.title: Re: SCP concept-The ring of mimicry
item.content:encoded:
I kinda like the core idea of this but it feels…narratively lacking: you have an object which can be dangerous, but which is kinda interesting in how it does that, and that's a good start. But for this to land right, you need to come up with a way to show us it being dangerous: it has to cause something to happen that we're scared of say.

Alternatively: lean into the containment issues; explore how the foundation can contain this, have the time taken for it to animate something start decreasing say and use that danger as the driving force for some kinda story about the foundation trying to figure out a more permanent solution.

At the end of the day: you're really trying to write a short story about a weird thing; not an encyclopedia entry on it. And you have the weird thing down fine, you just…need the story explaining why it's interesting and how the foundation interact with it, y'know?

item.title: Re: Trapped in the walkie-talkie (Search greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
When I said he has a shield, I mean that he isn't being affected by visual SCP because he's technically blind.

Yeah, I mean, I get this; I just don't really see what interesting stuff this lets you do? It's not like they can e.g. send him into Site-13 to explore it because y'know, he's stuck in a walkie-talkie and can't do anything without someone else around?

I think if I was to summarise how I feel about this as a concept: it feels like something that really needs to explore the emotional arc of the person in the walkie-talkie, where they go from initially really upset about their condition to like…accepting; but it feels like you don't really have a setup that really allows you to explore this easily.

Like, I don't dislike the idea of him putting a team together but I can't help but feel like someone stuck in a walkie-talkie is just…highly unsuited to actually doing this? Like, how do they know what's going on? How do they get in touch with their team if their team aren't by walkie-talkies? How do they do like…any of the paperwork expected of a team leader?

item.title: Re: What is Love?
item.content:encoded:
I really vibe with both the core idea of the SCP and the start of the narrative you have here; though my concerns are two fold:

  • Where does this story go? Like, what are you doing with this stalemate beyond pointing at it existing?
  • How are you telling this story?

My concern is that it'd be very easy to write a short paragraph or two explaining the stalemate and then call the job done; and it feels like this is something that really needs exploration in a big, long form work that really like, lets the reader see what all the factions think and how they got into this uneasy truce to contain this thing; and like, explore both the politicking and the effect of the SCP on the world?

item.title: Re: Concept: The Young God
item.content:encoded:
This feels like it has interesting elements that don't really go anywhere and it feels like it needs more narrative oomph as a result.

Like, the idea of the imaginary friends is cool, but they feel…very background-y and like they aren't really affecting the narrative as much as it feels like they should for this to work.

This is how I feel about a lot of this: the actual narrative doesn't really go anywhere beyond just kinda stating that 'oh there's more going on than it seems' spookily. It kinda reminds me in style of SCP-2662 except that actually like…builds up to a final conclusion and like, is really carried by the characterisation of the SCP? And my concern here is the testing focus means you'll attempt to carry this in a very 'look at how weird the transmutation is!' way, which I don't think will land because frankly it's a concept that has been done to death. Even testing has been overdone a lot; the existence of huge SCPs like SCP-914 and SCP-294 early in the history of the site means that test logs are real hard to pull off nowadays.

item.title: Re: Concept: Man-Made Behemoth
item.content:encoded:
There's something about this that doesn't really work for me and I can't quite put my finger on what it is. I think part of it is that it feels, somewhat similar to SCP-5031 but with a lot more focus on why the behemoth exists; but I think part of it is that the exploration of how it came to be feels very…passive?

Like there's a kinda, flow of us getting more information about the thing that recontextualises what it means to us but there's not really a strong hook that gets us invested in the reading to get to the ending reveal? There's not, for example, big stakes to make us want something to be resolved, or really a big mystery or anything so much as you going 'hah, you thought this was a monster? actually it was human all along!'.

I think like, spending more time developing the whole, character of the monster and like, the growth of them might be more effective? Really like, rely on the emotional arc of the story in the same way that 5031 works, y'know? Rather than spending a lot of time being like 'yes look at this monster'.

item.title: Re: City of normacy
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

The Foundations discovers an area that negates anomalous effects and memories or instructions relating to the anomalous

This is always a little tricky because it implies 'all anomalous effects work in the same way' which is weird because like…why do memetic effects, teleporting humans and replicating cake all work in the same way?

Forgetting about anomalous stuff in general feels weird too; like, it feels perhaps like this being a generic antimemetic thing that makes you forget about it would be a good way to keep the core of this without getting rid of all the narrative building off it?

Though this brings us onto the narrative: the first paragraph feels very promising; the effects expanding and the foundation struggling to handle the situation is a really great start. This comes crashing down when it turns into it really being focussed on 'what does the anomaly do' later on which feels…underwhelming? My advice is figure out a whole narrative arc from a beginning of 'the foundation doesn't understand it' to an ending where they manage to come up with some kind of containment that's some sort of horrible compromise.

I'm kinda…iffy on the anomalous human at the centre of this: it could be a good idea but it doesn't really feel like your summary hints at why it's important? It just kinda feels like there's a person at the centre, rather than all of the effects boiling down to being like…the persons guilt at hurting their family by reality bending and them trying to force anomalous behaviour to not work ever to protect everyone else, y'know?

item.title: Re: SCP-5632 Idea: A Word, if you will, about your transphobic B U L L S H I T
item.content:encoded:
This was created by an "anartist" who is all about practical stuff. Would probably involve exploration of Whiteboard Dimension to her old notes and such.

So, tell me about this: what do her old notes say? Why are they of interest now? What's in the whiteboard dimension that makes it interesting to explore?

I think my concern with this idea is that it's what I'd term 'overbroad': it's the kinda idea that opens you up to all kinds of cool and interesting things you could do with it, which in turn means finding the one that's actually interesting is really hard.

I like the idea of tying an anartist in here; and like, exploring what she got up to using this and stuff, but my largest concern is really just that I don't have a good idea of where this goes or anything. The actual whiteboard might be a touch overcomplex in how it works: it feels like it could be streamlined to have more focus with a few less anomalous bits to it but I don't think this is necessarily a huge issue as long as you do something interesting with it.
